newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex to take over Bis.
newsitem.headline: Vendex to take over Bis.

text.p: Dutch retail and business services group Vendex International NV said on Monday it planned to take over French temporary employment agency Bis.
Vendex said it had reached agreement with Bis founder Laurent Negro and his family to acquire their 60 percent stake in the company for 490 francs per share.
It said it would make a public bid soon at the same price for the remaining shares which are listed on the Paris bourse.
Bis has a total of 5.1 million shares outstanding, so the Vendex bid values the French company at 2.5 billion francs.
Vendex said the bid would be paid in cash from existing credit lines and would have a moderately positive effect on its earnings per share in the 1997/98 financial year.
The Dutch company said it was considering a separate Dutch bourse listing for its business services division whose annual turnover will more than double to over six billion guilders.
The separately listed company would be Europe's third biggest provider of temporary employment services and the continent's second biggest in commercial cleaning services.
Vendex said Bis made an operating profit of 141 million guilders and a net profit of 67 million in 1995 on turnover of some three billion guilders, though 1996 profits would be lower.
Bis is France's third biggest temporary help agency after Adecco and Manpower.
Vendex derived 1.9 billion guilders of its total 1995/96 turnover of 11.3 billion guilders from temporary help services.
Its Vedior temporary help unit is mainly active in the Benelux countries but already ranks fifth in France and also operates in Spain and Germany.
